title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: E is an elliptic curve over a field k of characteristic ≠ 2, and t_E is its tangent line at the origin. F_n = Γ(E, O(n·0_E)) is the space of functions with a pole of order ≤ n at the origin, so F_* is a filtered/graded algebra. The symbol map ε_n : F_n → t_E^{⊗n} (leading polar coefficient) gives F_n/F_{n-1} ≅ t_E^{⊗n}. The invariant derivation θ_δ (δ ∈ t_E) gives maps δ_n : t_E ⊗ F_n → F_{n+1}. The involution f ↦ f∘(−1) splits F_n = F_n^+ ⊕ F_n^- (previous page).

This page continues the coordinate-free Weierstrass theory.
(19) Even functions are functions on the quotient Σ_J = E/±1 ≅ P^1, where t is the image of 0_E and J is the set of images of the three nonzero 2-torsion points. Hence F_{2n}^+ = F_{2n+1}^+ = Γ(P^1, O(n·t)), of dimension n+1.
(20) F_n^- = 0 for n ≤ 2. F_3^- = δ_2(t_E ⊗ F_2) ≅ t_E^{⊗3} is a rank-1 complement of F_2 = F_3^+ in F_3.
(21) F_{2n+1}^- = F_{2n+2}^- ≅ F_3^- ⊗ F_{2n-2}^+: odd functions equal y times even functions.
(22–24) Choose δ ∈ t_E and p ∈ F_2 with ε_2(p) = δ^{⊗2}; this is ℘ (equivalently x) normalized by δ. Set p' = θ_δ p; this is ℘' (equivalently y).
(25, 25') Bases:
- {1, p, …, p^n} is a basis of F_{2n}^+.
- {p', p'p, …, p'p^{n-1}} is a basis of F_{2n+1}^-.
(26) F_{2n+1}^- = p'·F_{2n-2}^+.

Proposition 1: the evaluation map F_3 → k^J at the three nonzero 2-torsion points has kernel F_3^- = k·p'. Odd functions vanish at 2-torsion (proved on the next page). The map is injective on F_3^+ = ⟨1, p⟩ because the values p(J) (= e_1, e_2, e_3) are distinct; this is equivalent to a Vandermonde nondegeneracy. The next page then derives the Weierstrass cubic p'^2 = p^3 + a_1p^2 + a_2p + a_3.

Purpose: an intrinsic, t_E-equivariant construction of the Weierstrass and Legendre normal forms. This prepares a description of the moduli of elliptic curves with level-2 structure (J labelled 0, 1, ∞; λ ∈ P^1 − {0, 1, ∞}) in characteristic ≠ 2.
errors: Normalization in (24): if ε_2(p) = δ^{⊗2} (p ~ z^{-2} with δ(z) = 1), then θ_δ p ~ −2z^{-3}, so ε_3(p') = −2δ^{⊗3}, not δ^{⊗3}. The same happens with the classical ℘'^2 = 4℘^3 − …. The later relation (28), p'^2 = p^3 + …, is then off by the factor 4, unless the δ_n or ε conventions absorb a factor −n. This is a minor sign/constant slip; it is harmless in characteristic ≠ 2 since 2 is invertible.
Proposition 1 implicitly needs the 2-torsion points to be rational (k algebraically closed or full level-2 structure) so that J has 3 k-points; this is consistent with the context J = ₂E*.

ideas.what: Even/odd decomposition of Riemann–Roch spaces L(n·0) under [−1]; even part = Γ(P^1, O(n·t)) via E/±1 ≅ P^1
ideas.modern_name: Weierstrass/Riemann–Roch basis of L(n·O); quotient by inversion as double cover of P^1 branched at 2-torsion
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Weierstrass); standard in Silverman, Katz–Mazur, Deligne's 'Courbes elliptiques: formulaire'

ideas.what: Coordinate-free normalization of ℘, ℘' via a tangent vector δ ∈ t_E and the symbol ε_n: F_n → t_E^{⊗n}
ideas.modern_name: Weierstrass equation with ω-weights (modular forms as sections of ω^{⊗k}); invariant differential normalization

ideas.what: Kernel of evaluation at nonzero 2-torsion on L(3·0) is spanned by ℘'; values ℘(J) are distinct
ideas.modern_name: ℘' vanishes exactly at 2-torsion; e_1, e_2, e_3 distinct (nonzero discriminant)

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but entirely classical intrinsic rederivation of the Weierstrass normal form in characteristic ≠ 2. Nothing absent from the standard literature (Deligne's Formulaire, Katz–Mazur).
transcription_corrections: (19): '{\dagger}' should be '{t}' (t = image of 0_E in Σ_J, as defined on the previous page); i.e. Γ(Σ_J, n{t}).
The double arrows '⇒' in (19) and (21) are equality/isomorphism signs (F_{2n}^+ ≃ F_{2n+1}^+, F_{2n+1}^- ≃ F_{2n+2}^-).
(21): the right side is F_3^- ⊗_k F_{2n-2}^+ (the superscript on F_3 is '−', with a stray mark).
(25) first line reads 'F_2 = F_2^+ = F_3^+' as transcribed; fine.
